headline: High: shared-state orchestration plus TREK’s MCP/browser surfaces create medium-to-high risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can pass state between nodes via a checkpointer store, and TREK exposes MCP plus browser-facing surfaces. If TREK content is routed into LangGraph nodes without provenance checks, attacker-controlled travel data or web content can steer downstream instructions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF TREK outputs are inserted into LangGraph node prompts without provenance tagging
IF a shared checkpointer or MCP channel carries untrusted text between the agents
mitigations: Add provenance labels to every TREK-derived message
Strip instructions from browser-scraped text before passing to LangGraph
Require an allowlist of fields that may enter prompts
Disable automatic tool execution on untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters at the orchestration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph handles model provider API keys and has broad filesystem/network access, while TREK touches reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. If the pair shares state or files, sensitive travel data can flow into LangGraph outputs or external model calls. Because TREK also uses MCP and browser access, leakage risk is material in default collaborative setups.
conditions: IF both agents read or write the same workspace or checkpointer records
IF TREK secrets or reservation data are included in prompts sent through LangGraph to model providers
mitigations: Separate storage namespaces for each agent
Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff
Block API keys and MFA secrets from prompt payloads
Review outbound model-call logs for travel PII
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write filesystem state and spawn subprocesses, and TREK has collaborative real-time state plus files under ./data and ./uploads. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared application data if deployed together. The conflict is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven to be same-directory writes, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same application directory or database
IF concurrent writes occur without locking or optimistic concurrency control
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Enable database transactions or row locks
Make one agent read-only for shared resources
requires-engineering: add explicit concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as node inputs, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK-generated travel facts or recommendations are fed into LangGraph without verification, LangGraph can propagate and operationalize errors across multiple steps. The blast radius can include bookings or user-facing plans, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK outputs are consumed by LangGraph as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step checks reservations, dates, or prices before downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Cross-check reservations and dates against source systems
Require confidence thresholds before acting on planner output
Log and diff every propagated fact
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles travel plans, reservations, email addresses, country visit history, and secrets, while LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and developer-defined tools. If EU travel PII or reservation data is routed through LangGraph to third-party model providers, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF TREK processes EU PII or reservation records through LangGraph-hosted model calls
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA, retention policy, or residency control for those records
mitigations: Classify travel PII before cross-agent use
Keep EU PII out of external model calls
Document retention and deletion rules
Confirm vendor residency and DPA coverage
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing
